1565	/// The `Model::invoke` stream contract, checked against the Anthropic Messages
1566	/// API.
1567	///
1568	/// This is the provider whose truncation defect is half the reason this suite
1569	/// exists: SMA-531 (PR #200), where a stream that ended cleanly between
1570	/// `message_delta` and `message_stop` emitted `Usage` and then nothing —
1571	/// `MessageTranslator`'s buffered stop reason was never flushed, so the
1572	/// consumer got no terminal event at all. `TruncatedAfterStopReason` below
1573	/// reproduces that shape — the same event sequence, through `message_delta`'s
1574	/// `stop_reason`/`usage` values — from the fixture the SMA-531 fix itself is
1575	/// tested against; see the Fixture provenance section below for what this
1576	/// module substitutes rather than transcribes.
1577	///
1578	/// # Fixture provenance
1579	///
1580	/// Every envelope shape below is transcribed from a fixture committed in
1581	/// `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/`, cited on the
1582	/// helper or script arm that builds it:
1583	///
1584	/// - `text_only.txt` — the baseline: `message_start` (including its top-level
1585	///   `"stop_reason":null`), a text `content_block_start`, two
1586	///   `content_block_delta`s, `content_block_stop`, `message_delta`
1587	///   (`stop_reason` + `usage` in one event), `message_stop`. Grounds
1588	///   [`message_start`], [`content_block_start_text`], [`text_delta`],
1589	///   [`content_block_stop`], [`message_delta`] and [`message_stop`], and
1590	///   `CleanStop`'s full script.
1591	/// - `eof_after_message_delta.txt` — the exact SMA-531 shape and the fixture
1592	///   the crate's own `clean_eof_after_message_delta_emits_finish` regression
1593	///   test reads: `text_only.txt`'s prefix through `message_delta`, then the
1594	///   body simply ends — no `message_stop`. `TruncatedAfterStopReason` draws
1595	///   its event sequence and `message_delta`'s `stop_reason`/`usage` values
1596	///   from this fixture (via `through_stop()`, with no `message_stop`
1597	///   appended); `message_start`'s `id`/`model` and the delta text are this
1598	///   module's own constants, not the fixture's literal values (see
1599	///   [`message_start`]'s doc).
1600	/// - `eof_mid_content_block.txt` — grounds `TruncatedMidGeneration`'s
1601	///   envelope shape (`message_start`, `content_block_start`, a
1602	///   `content_block_delta`, then EOF with no `message_delta` at all). The
1603	///   delta *count* is not grounded from this file — as with every other
1604	///   subject in this module, `opening()`'s two deltas are arbitrary content
1605	///   over a grounded envelope, not a literal transcription.
1606	/// - `stream_error.txt` — grounds `ErrorMidGeneration`'s prefix envelope
1607	///   (`message_start`, `content_block_start`, one `content_block_delta`)
1608	///   *before* its own in-band `event: error` frame. See "Why `Ending::Abort`
1609	///   and not the fixtures' own `error` event" below for why that frame itself
1610	///   is not transcribed into this script.
1611	/// - `error_after_message_delta.txt` — grounds `ErrorAfterStopReason`'s
1612	///   prefix envelope: the same event-sequence shape as
1613	///   `eof_after_message_delta.txt`'s through `message_delta` (message_start,
1614	///   content_block_start, delta(s), content_block_stop, message_delta),
1615	///   though the two fixtures are not byte-identical to each other — this one
1616	///   carries a different `message_start` id and one delta where the other
1617	///   has two — again *before* its own in-band `error` frame.
1618	/// - `parallel_tool_use.txt` and `tool_use_then_continuation.txt` — the
1619	///   `tool_use` envelope: a `content_block_start` carrying the whole `id` and
1620	///   `name` together, followed by exactly one `input_json_delta` carrying the
1621	///   whole argument JSON. Grounds [`tool_use_start`], [`input_json_delta`],
1622	///   and `ToolCallCleanStop`'s script.
1623	///
1624	/// `body_cut_inside_message_stop.txt` and `thinking_then_text.txt` were read
1625	/// but contribute no shape this module needs: the former is a byte-level cut
1626	/// of `eof_after_message_delta.txt` that the SSE parser discards down to the
1627	/// same events (already covered), and this suite has no reasoning-delta
1628	/// scenario for any subject.
1629	///
1630	/// # Why `Ending::Abort` and not the fixtures' own `error` event
1631	///
1632	/// `stream_error.txt` and `error_after_message_delta.txt` both encode
1633	/// Anthropic's real error mechanism: an in-band `event: error` SSE frame,
1634	/// parsed by `AnthropicEvent::Error` and turned into `Err(ModelError::…)` by
1635	/// `stream.rs`'s `consume`. That path is already exercised directly against
1636	/// the translator by the crate's own
1637	/// `stream_error_overloaded_terminates_with_unavailable` and
1638	/// `error_after_buffered_stop_reason_emits_no_finish` tests.
1639	///
1640	/// This module instead scripts `ErrorMidGeneration` and `ErrorAfterStopReason`
1641	/// with the harness's `Ending::Abort` — a raw transport-level disconnect, no
1642	/// `error` frame on the wire at all — matching exactly how `bedrock`,
1643	/// `openai_chat` and `litellm` script the same two scenarios. That keeps this
1644	/// suite testing the property it exists to test (the driver's `tokio::select!`
1645	/// cancel/error arms in `model.rs`, and specifically that a buffered stop
1646	/// reason is discarded rather than flushed when the transport fails) the same
1647	/// way across every subject, rather than re-deriving Anthropic's in-band error
1648	/// shape a second time in a different harness. Functionally the two
1649	/// mechanisms are indistinguishable to this driver either way: `model.rs`'s
1650	/// `Some(Err(e)) => { yield Err(...); return; }` arm returns as soon as it
1651	/// observes *any* transport-level error, before it would ever get to parse a
1652	/// subsequent `error` frame.
1653	///
1654	/// # Three things specific to this provider
1655	///
1656	/// **`message_delta` carries the stop reason AND usage in the same event**
1657	/// (see [`message_delta`]'s doc). That is what gives `CancelAfterStopReason` an
1658	/// observable edge to gate on at all — unlike `openai_chat`/`litellm`, whose
1659	/// finish-reason chunk is silent and needs a synthetic *following* usage chunk
1660	/// for the gate to sit after.
1661	///
1662	/// **`message_start` also emits a `Usage`** (`stream.rs`'s `MessageStart` arm),
1663	/// which makes the harness's own "at least one `Usage` observed" floor for
1664	/// `CancelAfterStopReason` vacuous for this subject — it is satisfied by
1665	/// `message_start` alone, whether or not the gate sits in the right place. The
1666	/// harness's `floor_violation` doc records this narrowing explicitly. The only
1667	/// guard left for this scenario on this subject is the provenance comment on
1668	/// its `script` match arm below, which states in prose where `gate_after`
1669	/// counts to and why — treat that comment as load-bearing, not decoration.
1670	///
1671	/// **`message_start` contains a literal `"stop_reason":null`.** A naive scan
1672	/// for the substring `stop_reason` would therefore match the very first event
1673	/// of every script, whether or not a stop reason was ever encoded.
1674	/// [`STOP_REASON_MARKER`] scans for the populated-string shape instead, pinned
1675	/// against `message_start`'s `null` by `scan_finds_only_a_populated_stop_reason`
1676	/// — the only detector for `ErrorAfterStopReason` degrading into
1677	/// `ErrorMidGeneration`: `classify` and `floor_violation` don't distinguish
1678	/// the two by `Usage` count, only by `Finish`/`Err` presence and ordering,
1679	/// which already match for both (see `scan_finds_only_a_populated_stop_reason`'s
1680	/// own doc for the full argument).
1681	///
1682	/// # `ToolCallCleanStop` never splits `input_json_delta`
1683	///
1684	/// Every committed tool-call fixture (`parallel_tool_use.txt`,
1685	/// `tool_use_then_continuation.txt`) carries one tool call's whole argument
1686	/// JSON in a single `input_json_delta`. Unlike `bedrock`/`openai_chat`/
1687	/// `litellm`, this module does not split the arguments across two calls to its
1688	/// delta helper to *additionally* prove "not more than one delta carries the
1689	/// name" — no committed capture grounds Anthropic ever doing that, and
1690	/// inventing the split would fabricate a shape per this file's provenance
1691	/// rule. A single `input_json_delta` still fully exercises assertion 7's
1692	/// "exactly one, not zero" on this shape: the translator's `name_emitted` flag
1693	/// starts `false`, so the one delta this script sends is the one that must
1694	/// carry the name.
1695	mod anthropic {
1696	    use super::*;
1697	    use paigasus_helikon_providers_anthropic::AnthropicModel;
1698	
1699	    /// The model id `build_model_against` requests. Matches the constructor
1700	    /// example in the task brief (`AnthropicModel::messages("claude-3-5-sonnet-latest")`).
1701	    const MODEL_ID: &str = "claude-3-5-sonnet-latest";
1702	
1703	    /// The tool name every tool-call fixture declares.
1704	    const TOOL_NAME: &str = "get_weather";
1705	
1706	    /// `id` for the single tool call in the tool fixture. Not claimed to match
1707	    /// any real Anthropic id format (`tu_weather`/`tu_a`/`tu_b` is the shape
1708	    /// `parallel_tool_use.txt` and `tool_use_then_continuation.txt` use, but
1709	    /// nothing under test inspects it) — fixed purely so failure output is
1710	    /// stable and greppable.
1711	    const TOOL_USE_ID: &str = "tu_conformance_0";
1712	
1713	    /// The substring that appears in a chunk if and only if it carries a
1714	    /// *populated* `stop_reason`.
1715	    ///
1716	    /// The obvious marker — `stop_reason` alone — is wrong for this subject:
1717	    /// `message_start` carries an explicit `"stop_reason":null` at the top
1718	    /// level of its `message` object (see [`message_start`], grounded in
1719	    /// `text_only.txt`), so a bare substring scan would report a stop reason
1720	    /// on the very first event of every script, whether or not one was ever
1721	    /// encoded. Scanning for the opening quote of a *string* value excludes
1722	    /// the null case: `null` has no quote after the colon, `"end_turn"`/
1723	    /// `"tool_use"` do. `scan_finds_only_a_populated_stop_reason` is the guard
1724	    /// that keeps this true, including against `message_start`'s literal
1725	    /// `null`.
1726	    const STOP_REASON_MARKER: &[u8] = b"\"stop_reason\":\"";
1727	
1728	    /// One SSE frame: `event: {event}\ndata: {payload}\n\n`. Anthropic frames
1729	    /// carry an explicit event name — unlike the bare `data:` frames OpenAI
1730	    /// and LiteLLM send — matching every fixture in this crate's own
1731	    /// `tests/fixtures/`.
1732	    ///
1733	    /// The `event:` line is cosmetic to the translator: `model.rs` parses
1734	    /// `event.data` alone via `AnthropicEvent`'s `#[serde(tag = "type")]`,
1735	    /// never `event.event`. It is still written here because every real
1736	    /// Anthropic response sends it, and a fixture that omitted it would not be
1737	    /// the stream it claims to be.
1738	    fn frame(event: &str, payload: serde_json::Value) -> Vec<u8> {
1739	        format!("event: {event}\ndata: {payload}\n\n").into_bytes()
1740	    }
1741	
1742	    /// `message_start`, which opens every Anthropic stream and is the event
1743	    /// the translator reads its initial `Usage` from
1744	    /// (`stream.rs`'s `MessageStart` arm).
1745	    ///
1746	    /// Matches `text_only.txt`'s opening event, including the top-level
1747	    /// `"stop_reason":null` on the `message` object — the shape
1748	    /// [`STOP_REASON_MARKER`] must not match.
1749	    fn message_start() -> Vec<u8> {
1750	        frame(
1751	            "message_start",
1752	            json!({
1753	                "type": "message_start",
1754	                "message": {
1755	                    "id": "msg_conformance",
1756	                    "type": "message",
1757	                    "role": "assistant",
1758	                    "content": [],
1759	                    "model": MODEL_ID,
1760	                    "stop_reason": null,
1761	                    "usage": {
1762	                        "input_tokens": 12,
1763	                        "cache_read_input_tokens": 0,
1764	                        "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0,
1765	                        "output_tokens": 0
1766	                    }
1767	                }
1768	            }),
1769	        )
1770	    }
1771	
1772	    /// `content_block_start` opening a text block. Matches `text_only.txt`'s
1773	    /// second event. The translator's `ContentBlockStart`/`Text` arm records
1774	    /// no `ModelEvent` for this; it is included because a real stream opens
1775	    /// every block it later closes.
1776	    fn content_block_start_text() -> Vec<u8> {
1777	        frame(
1778	            "content_block_start",
1779	            json!({
1780	                "type": "content_block_start",
1781	                "index": 0,
1782	                "content_block": { "type": "text", "text": "" }
1783	            }),
1784	        )
1785	    }
1786	
1787	    /// One text delta. Envelope matches `text_only.txt`'s delta events; the
1788	    /// content itself is arbitrary, as in every other subject in this file.
1789	    fn text_delta(text: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
1790	        frame(
1791	            "content_block_delta",
1792	            json!({
1793	                "type": "content_block_delta",
1794	                "index": 0,
1795	                "delta": { "type": "text_delta", "text": text }
1796	            }),
1797	        )
1798	    }
1799	
1800	    /// `content_block_stop`, closing the block opened above. Matches
1801	    /// `text_only.txt`. Ignored by the translator
1802	    /// (`AnthropicEvent::ContentBlockStop { .. }` only logs); included because
1803	    /// a real stream closes every block it opens.
1804	    fn content_block_stop() -> Vec<u8> {
1805	        frame(
1806	            "content_block_stop",
1807	            json!({ "type": "content_block_stop", "index": 0 }),
1808	        )
1809	    }
1810	
1811	    /// `message_delta` — the one event that carries BOTH the stop reason and
1812	    /// usage in a single frame. Matches `text_only.txt`'s and
1813	    /// `eof_after_message_delta.txt`'s shared shape.
1814	    ///
1815	    /// This is the load-bearing difference from every other subject in this
1816	    /// file: `stream.rs`'s `MessageDelta` arm emits `Usage` from the same
1817	    /// event that buffers `stop_reason`, so this event is itself an
1818	    /// observable edge a cancellation can gate on — unlike `openai_chat`/
1819	    /// `litellm`, whose finish-reason chunk is silent and needs a *following*
1820	    /// usage chunk to give `CancelAfterStopReason` something to gate on.
1821	    fn message_delta(stop_reason: &str, output_tokens: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
1822	        frame(
1823	            "message_delta",
1824	            json!({
1825	                "type": "message_delta",
1826	                "delta": { "stop_reason": stop_reason, "stop_sequence": null },
1827	                "usage": { "output_tokens": output_tokens }
1828	            }),
1829	        )
1830	    }
1831	
1832	    /// `message_stop`, which flushes the buffered stop reason into `Finish`
1833	    /// (`stream.rs`'s `MessageStop` arm). Matches `text_only.txt`.
1834	    fn message_stop() -> Vec<u8> {
1835	        frame("message_stop", json!({ "type": "message_stop" }))
1836	    }
1837	
1838	    /// `content_block_start` opening a `tool_use` block. Matches
1839	    /// `parallel_tool_use.txt`'s and `tool_use_then_continuation.txt`'s
1840	    /// tool-call events. The translator records `call_id`/`name` here but
1841	    /// emits nothing — the name-carrying `ToolCallDelta` comes with the first
1842	    /// `input_json_delta` — which is why `FragmentedToolName` is declined for
1843	    /// this subject: the name arrives whole, in this one event.
1844	    fn tool_use_start(call_id: &str, name: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
1845	        frame(
1846	            "content_block_start",
1847	            json!({
1848	                "type": "content_block_start",
1849	                "index": 0,
1850	                "content_block": { "type": "tool_use", "id": call_id, "name": name, "input": {} }
1851	            }),
1852	        )
1853	    }
1854	
1855	    /// One `input_json_delta`, carrying a whole argument JSON. See the module
1856	    /// doc's "`ToolCallCleanStop` never splits `input_json_delta`" section for
1857	    /// why this is never called twice for one call in this module, unlike its
1858	    /// siblings' tool-argument helpers.
1859	    fn input_json_delta(partial_json: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
1860	        frame(
1861	            "content_block_delta",
1862	            json!({
1863	                "type": "content_block_delta",
1864	                "index": 0,
1865	                "delta": { "type": "input_json_delta", "partial_json": partial_json }
1866	            }),
1867	        )
1868	    }

1871	    /// `FragmentedToolName`, which this subject declines.
1872	    ///
1873	    /// Returning an `Option` rather than panicking on the declined scenario is
1874	    /// what lets [`Anthropic::encodes_stop_reason`] call this for *every*
1875	    /// scenario and measure the bytes — see `bedrock::script`'s doc for the
1876	    /// same pattern.

  collapsed into a flat `object` whose `properties` union the variants' fields
  and whose shared tag key becomes an `enum` of variant names.

This means schemars-derived schemas for tagged enums and generic structs pass

34	- **`RunContext<Ctx>`** — the per-run state shared across loop, tools, guardrails, and hooks (user context, `Session` handle, `HookRegistry`, `TracerHandle`, `CancellationToken`). Build with `RunContext::new(user_ctx, session, hooks, tracer, cancel)` (all five arguments explicit) or use `RunContext::ephemeral(user_ctx)` as the shorthand for the all-defaults case (in-memory session, empty hooks, default tracer, fresh cancel token); individual parts can then be overridden with the consuming setters `.with_session(...)`, `.with_hooks(...)`, `.with_tracer(...)`, `.with_cancel(...)`. **`RunConfig`** carries per-run knobs (`max_turns`, `timeout`, `parallel_tool_call_limit`, `max_agent_depth`). **`RunResult<T>`** (and its streaming counterpart `RunResultStreaming`) aggregate the run's `final_output`, `events`, and `TokenUsage`.
35	- **Event and item carriers** — `AgentEvent` is the unified stream variant emitted by every `Agent` (lifecycle, raw `TokenDelta` / `ReasoningDelta` / `ToolCallDelta`, semantic `MessageOutput` / `ToolCallItem` / `ToolOutputItem`, `HandoffItem`, control signals, and terminal `RunCompleted` / `RunFailed` / `RunDeferred` / `RunStopped`). `Item` / `ContentPart` are the conversation-message carriers; `ModelEvent`, `ModelRequest`, and `ToolDef` cross the model boundary; `SessionEvent` is the log entry a `Session` persists.
36	- **Provider data** — `ContentPart::ProviderData { provider, call_id, data }` carries opaque data that one provider translator owns, for example a Gemini `thoughtSignature`. A model reports it with `ModelEvent::ProviderData`. The rules are these:
37	  - `provider` is a wire-format key that one translator owns. It is not the value of `Model::provider()`. Each provider crate that writes provider data exports its key as a `pub const`. The Gemini crate exports `PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` (`"gemini"`). A host can use the key to filter or remove the data.
38	  - A translator reads only the parts with its own key. It ignores every other part without a warning, and it never fails because of one.
39	  - The part is valid only inside an `Item::AssistantMessage`. Every translator ignores it in any other item.
40	  - `call_id: Some(id)` means the data belongs to the tool call with that id in the same model response. That call is an `Item::ToolCall` that follows the message, or a `ContentPart::ToolUse` in the same message. Call ids can repeat across responses.
41	  - The position of the part in `content` has no meaning. The parts keep their arrival order among themselves. A provider that needs block structure stores the whole block in `data`.
42	  - `Item::is_provider_data_only()` is true for an assistant message that holds only provider data. Such a message has no text for a reader, and a text consumer can skip it.
43	  - **Rollback note:** a reader on an earlier core version fails on `provider_data` with "unknown variant". After the first turn that stores this variant, a session store or a Temporal history holds it. Deploy readers and Temporal workflow workers before writers. Do not roll back core below this version on a deployment that stored such a turn.

#### JSON-Schema sanitizer

A JSON-Schema sanitizer runs automatically on every schema passed to
`responseSchema`. It inlines `$ref` references, converts `[T, "null"]` type
arrays to `nullable: true`, replaces `const` with single-item `enum`, renames
`oneOf` to `anyOf`, strips unsupported keywords (`$schema`,
`additionalProperties`, `unevaluatedProperties`, `patternProperties`,
`examples`, `default`, `$defs`/`definitions`), and drops `format` values Gemini
doesn't recognize for their type (keeping e.g. `enum`/`date-time`). Schemars-
derived schemas for typical Rust structs and enums pass without manual adjustment.

#### Limitations

Remote-URL images, audio parts, and non-text tool-result parts are silently
dropped during request translation. Reasoning streaming (`ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta`)
is not yet emitted by this provider.

Tool loops on Gemini 3 work. Gemini 3 returns a `thoughtSignature` with a
tool call and rejects the next request if the signature is missing. The
provider keeps each signature as `ContentPart::ProviderData` (key
`PROVIDER_DATA_KEY`, value `"gemini"`) and sends it back on its own call. It
also restores the call order that Gemini returned. For a call of the current
turn that has no valid signature, it sends the documented dummy value
`skip_thought_signature_validator`. A signature from another model id or
another API counts as not valid. The dummy is sent only for Gemini 3 and later
ids. Gemini 1.x and 2.x requests keep their earlier shape and get no dummy.
For Gemini 3 and later, a request that ends with a model turn gets a `user` text turn "Continue." appended, because Gemini rejects such a request.
These limits apply:

- Vertex signatures are not live-tested.
- The dummy value is live-tested only on `gemini-3.8-flash` (Developer API).
  It is not tested on Gemini 2.x (these ids return 404 for new users) or on
  Vertex.
- Text-level signatures are not sent back.

Gemini bills signatures as input tokens, so provider data adds to the prompt
size.

> Model ids are illustrative — swap them for any model your account can reach.

Gemini does not use provider tool types. It sends the generic schema for every tool. See [Provider tool types](./tools.md#provider-tool-types).

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The stream half and the data model are sound. Goal 4 keeps the stored format and the next request of every turn without thinking unchanged. The request half is not specified well enough to build, and two decisions rest on evidence that differs from what the SDK sends or what core produces. Close the two BLOCKERs before implementation starts. Each needs a short probe and explicit rules, not a new approach.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

- **Thinking-only assistant messages are a new wire shape that core makes on normal paths, and no probe covers them**
  - What is wrong:
    - On `main`, an `AssistantMessage` with only `Reasoning` and provider data gives no blocks. The translator treats it as absent (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-840/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs:89-92). After this change it gives `[thinking]`, and the translator sends it.
    - Core makes this shape in normal use. `thread_handoff_transcript` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-840/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:766-789, called at loop_state.rs:319 and /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-840/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs:603) removes every `ToolCall`/`ToolResult` but keeps assistant messages. So the hand-off turn `[thinking, tool_use transfer_to_x]` becomes `[thinking]`.
    - A `Length` finish after the thinking block, or a blank text, gives the same shape. `claude-sonnet-5-5` is not in `KNOWN_MODELS`, so it gets `max_tokens` 4096 (capabilities.rs:18-23), and adaptive thinking can use all of it.
    - No probe row covers "thinking kept, its `tool_use` and `tool_result` removed", and no row covers "assistant message with only thinking blocks".

### QUESTIONS
- Should a text-only turn with thinking write provider data, or only a `tool_use` turn? SMA-827 wrote Gemini data on tool turns only, so that text turns keep the earlier stored format. On models before Opus 4.5 the API removes the thinking of earlier turns, so the only gain there is a stable cache prefix.
- Does Anthropic accept thinking blocks for a model with no thinking support? `claude-3-5-haiku-*` and `claude-3-*` are in `KNOWN_MODELS`. `CompactingSession` sends the full history to its own `model` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-840/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/compacting_session.rs:200-211), and that is often a cheaper model. On `main` that request has no thinking blocks.
- Is a signature bound to an organization, a workspace, or an API key? If yes, a session that moves to another key gets the permanent failure from the MAJOR finding on recovery.
- The "Thinking blocks removed" row returned 200, and in pass B the model did not think again. Is this the documented behaviour in which the API turns off thinking for that request? If yes, write it into Finding 1. It means that today's loop runs but stops thinking after the first tool call, and that is the real gain of this change for users.

## What's good
- Goal 4 and its buffering rule. A response with no thinking writes no provider data, so turns without thinking keep their stored format and next request. Users with `ExtendedThinking::Disabled`, the default, see no change.
- The probe came first, its results table is clear, and it states its limits ("one sample only"). The cross-model row and the order row support the "no model check" non-goal with more evidence than SMA-827 had for Gemini.
- The design uses the SMA-827 carrier again with no core change. The tool positions are keyed to `call_id` and gated on `name_emitted`, so they agree with assertion 8. The key constant is separate from `PROVIDER_ID`.
